notes: Closed all 11 findings from hydrogen (F1-F11) via direct edits, theorem refinements, estimator corrections, recall classification, and a 25-item harder robustness run; verified all 412 claims, 31 source claims, and 21 rendered PDF pages with two minor remaining items (n=6->7 estimator step in plotted curves and omitted 'suffix: III' on dellacqua2026).

contribution.assessment: Building on Davis et al. (2024) and Stroebl et al. (2024), the paper frames verifier-limited resampling through attainable sets, finite-compute odds-ratio thresholds (Proposition 2), a covariance identity separating pooled precision from the abstaining ceiling plus a mean-preserving spread ordering (Proposition 3 and Rothschild & Stiglitz 1970), and candidate re-verification under correlated verdicts (Proposition 4, untested). The expanded empirical study covers 40 main HMMT problems and 25 harder Omni-MATH problems on frozen outputs, but remains small, leaves most main-set check differences unresolved from zero and the harder-set self-check gain (+0.022) non-significant, and documents substantial benchmark memorization (>=30% and >=67% explicit recall in the stronger model's verdicts), leaving the overall contribution as a useful synthesis.
